text:
cs_jordan: @eng_sam heads-up — Ivyton reports p99 jumps around 18:05 UTC. Customer says it started after a marketing batch. They hit several 8–12s responses on /v1/generate. sample req id: req_ivy_0a1b2c

customer_ivyton_sre: Confirming — we saw a spike at ~18:03, mostly on multi-turn chat with long contexts. p95 ~600ms but p99 up to 11s. No auth errors, just slow tails.

infra_bot: [alert] tenant=ivyton p99_generation >= 8s for 15m (rule: tenant-p99-high) — incident ticket: INC-21499 created.

eng_sam: Thanks. Can you paste a minimal repro (prompt + params) and a request id that failed? Also which model variant are they using (gptx-medium-8q?)

customer_ivyton_sre: Repro snippet: `POST /v1/generate` body: `{ "model": "gptx-medium-8q", "input": "<conversation of ~6 messages, ~2400 tokens>", "max_tokens": 512, "stream": false }`. Failed req: `req_ivy_0a1b2c`.

eng_sam: Running traces now. Quick check of routing/history: their requests routed to pool=dedicated-us-east-3, node set xgpu-12. No recent deploys.

eng_sam: Metric dump for req_ivy_0a1b2c: `kernel_queue_wait=980ms, kv_cache_load=45ms, token_compute=6s, post_process=600ms` — token_compute dominated.

sre_lina: Token_compute at 6s suggests contention on that GPU for long-seq workloads. Any co-located tenants pushing high prefix lengths?

eng_sam: Looking at tenant heatmap for the pool: another tenant (bakerylabs) had a burst of bulk-embeds around 18:00 — lots of long sequences and interleaving. bakerylabs had many short-lived high-concurrency streams. That matches noisy-neighbor pattern.

customer_ivyton_sre: Bakerylabs is a different customer, can we isolate Ivyton? They are on Dedicated but not fully isolated from soft-shares. We need something quick, our SLA customer is impacted.

sre_lina: Immediate mitigations we can try: 1) temp soft-isolate Ivyton -> set tenant_priority=high for scheduling (priority lane). 2) Apply a per-tenant concurrency cap for bakerylabs to smooth interleaving. 3) If available, move Ivyton to a reserved slot or small reservation in the pool. Any preference?

eng_sam: I can flip a scheduling flag to pin Ivyton requests to lower-concurrency lanes and reduce interleaving. Command (internal):
```
POST /internal/v1/tenants/ivyton/policy
{ "scheduling": { "priority_lane": true, "max_inflight": 12 }}
```
I'll also throttle bakerylabs to cap concurrency to 20 for 30m:
```
POST /internal/v1/tenants/bakerylabs/policy
{ "scheduling": { "max_inflight": 20, "burst_window_sec": 60 }}
```

eng_sam: Applying now.

infra_bot: [action] scheduling policy applied for tenant=ivyton by eng_sam at 18:24 UTC.

eng_sam: Applied bakerylabs cap as well. Watching metrics.

(2m later)
eng_sam: Early telemetry: Ivyton p99 dropped from ~9.8s -> ~1.6s in the last 2 minutes. p95 stable ~500–650ms. Looks promising.

customer_ivyton_sre: Saw improvement on our end. Thanks. Any root cause follow-up to avoid recurrence?

sre_lina: Root cause: noisy neighbor caused GPU compute contention for long-seq workloads due to heavy interleaving and lack of tenant-level soft isolation. Follow-ups:
- create a scheduled job to detect high-interleaving bursts and auto-enact soft-isolate (priority lanes) when pool p99 > 2s for a tenant for >=5m.
- improve default per-tenant concurrency heuristics based on seq-length distribution.
- consider a burst-reservation API so customers can request short-term dedicated capacity (automated).

eng_sam: We'll open a backlog ticket to implement the auto-soft-isolate rule + metric alert tuning. Ticket: INF-5427. Also recommend customer-level guidance: prefer streaming mode for long-turn workloads to reduce token_compute blocking, or request a burst-reservation for campaigns.

customer_ivyton_sre: We'll evaluate streaming and plan to request reservations for future campaigns. Appreciate the quick fix. :thumbsup:

cs_jordan: Marking resolved for now. I'll follow up with Ivyton with postmortem and suggested mitigations.

sre_lina: Leaving a note: avoid long synchronous max_tokens for heavy campaigns if you don't have reservation — streaming or smaller chunks are safer.

eng_sam: Closing incident INC-21499 as mitigated; will update INF-5427 when we have a patch.

cs_jordan: Thanks everyone.
